newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks extend slide, NYSE sets trading curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks extend slide, NYSE sets trading curbs.

text.p: U.S. stocks slid further in early trading on Monday, still wary after strong economic data released on Friday gave new life to worries about higher interest rates and inflation.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was off 44 points, or 0.54 percent, to 8150. The New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 1006 EDT/1406 GMT.

The long bond, which tumbled on Friday after the release of above-forecast jobs data for July and a sharp rise in the National Association of Purchasing Management index, extended losses. It lost 14/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
"The bond market is still under some pressure," said Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony. "With the bond market acting weak, we are getting hit in equities markets."
The Nasdaq composite, which made a short-lived and early push to positive ground, fell three points to 1592.
Among economic data, the Commerce Department reported seasonally adjusted construction spending fell 1.1 percent in June compared with a revised 0.3 percent rise in May.
